clue.text: I tend not to mind knocking off early at work, not at all

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being rearranged, so the fodder is reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: knocking off work early means stopping before the end, so the final letter of mind goes

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed
the last letter of mind, cut off

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they don't mind slipping away from the office early, not one bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking off early' cuts MIND to MIN; 'at work' then shuffles I TEND NOT TO MIN into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the polite reply to thanks, meaning the favour was no trouble whatsoever.

clue.text: A mirror's shattering interrupts dull morning letter opening

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: dead means dull, lifeless

indicators.note: a mirror that shatters breaks into pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
AM is the abbreviation for morning (ante meridiem)

explanation.surface: A broken mirror spoils a dreary morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter opening' sounds like slitting an envelope, but it means the salutation a letter opens with. 'shattering' shuffles A MIRRORS into RSIRORM, which 'interrupts' the word for dull.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal salutation that begins a business letter to an unknown recipient.

clue.text: Call from high court judge deceived from below

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from below means the letters run upwards, so the phrase is turned round

parts.note: put on, as in 'you're putting me on', means deceived or fooled

explanation.surface: A senior judge calls out something misleading from the floor below.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'high court judge' is not a lawyer but a tennis umpire perched in a high chair beside the court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an umpire calls this when a player reaches the ball only after its second bounce.

clue.text: Capacity to recall any more MPs under review

indicators.note: something under review is being reconsidered and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Politicians being examined on how much they can remember about anything further.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory span is a psychology term for how many items a person can hold in mind at once.

clue.text: Surfer heading for Newquay gets size tens unpacked

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Newquay

indicators.note: unpacking removes the outer wrapping, so each of the three words loses its first and last letters

parts.note: gets without its outer letters
size without its outer letters
tens without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Cornish surfer arrives with large shoes and takes them out of the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Newquay is a Cornish surfing resort, which makes 'Surfer' look like a wave rider; here it is someone browsing the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A netizen is an active internet user, one who surfs the web.

clue.text: Works bar on Northern Irish peninsula

parts.note: an inn is a pub, a bar
the Ards Peninsula is in County Down, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Construction work at a pub on a peninsula in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The innards of a machine are its internal mechanism, its works.

clue.text: A, perhaps, with or without IOU?

definitions.text: A, perhaps, with or without IOU?

parts.words: A, perhaps, with or without IOU
parts.note: A is a musical tone, and an IOU is itself a promissory one; read the other way, A with I, O and U is every vowel bar E

explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT E: the vowels A, I, O, U are all of them except E. Without the IOU, A is still a musical tone, and an IOU is a written promise, so every reading lands on one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A is a musical tone, and an IOU is a written promise to pay; both are called by this word.

clue.text: Male pro attending party boosted our defenders

indicators.note: attending here means being present at the party, so the male pro goes inside it
boosted means pushed up, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
he is the male pronoun
for means in favour of, pro

explanation.surface: A man in favour of going to the party was given a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed services, collectively, are those who defend the nation.

clue.text: Sweet orchestral suite played without one?

indicators.note: music that is played is performed, and the letters are performed in a new order
without says a letter of the fodder is left out of the shuffle

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An orchestral suite performed without one musician, perhaps a missing player.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of ORCHESTRAL SUITE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte russe is a cold dessert of Bavarian cream set in a ring of sponge fingers.

clue.text: Fruit carried by single Anglo-French drone?

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the fruit sits within the other letters

parts.note: a single thing is 'a' in English and 'un' in French
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A lone cross-Channel drone delivers fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' does double duty across the languages: the English article and the French one, side by side, carry the fruit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a mechanical robot, and a drone is a person who works mindlessly like one.

clue.text: Committee that has enough power to be effective

indicators.note: has means contains, so the answer is held within the clue words before it

parts.note: the answer is inside these words

explanation.surface: A committee with sufficient authority to get things done.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or body with teeth has real force, the clout to make its rulings stick.

clue.text: Strange in Morse's case, man enjoying ale when a penny drops

indicators.note: drops means falls out, so the letter for a penny is removed

parts.note: a supper is one who sups, drinking ale
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: An odd case for Inspector Morse: a drinker realises something when the penny drops.
explanation.walkthrough: Chief Superintendent Strange is Morse's boss in the ITV detective series Inspector Morse, so he is the super.
explanation.definitionFit: Superintendent is the police rank, informally shortened, held by Strange over Morse.

clue.text: No time now for operation?

parts.note: zero means none, no amount
an hour is a period of time

explanation.surface: A patient told there is no time left before surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero hour is the moment a military operation is scheduled to start.

clue.text: See 12
Provider of zest in cocktail or water in spirit

indicators.note: in puts the water inside the spirit

parts.note: an angel is a heavenly spirit
pee is informal for urine, as in 'pass water'

explanation.surface: Bartender's instruction: zest the cocktail, or add water to the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Strips of citrus rind supply the zest twisted into many cocktails.

clue.text: US singer prepared to open Parliament?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Paul ..., the American bass-baritone
second meaning: read as ..., dressed in the ceremonial garb for the State Opening of Parliament

explanation.walkthrough: The State Opening of Parliament is the UK ceremony at which the monarch and peers wear formal robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Robeson was the American singer famous for 'Ol' Man River'; robed peers are ready for the State Opening.

clue.text: Maybe iron, copper and others supporting beams in disrepair

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits underneath the rest
beams in disrepair are broken and out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
et al is the Latin abbreviation for 'and others'

explanation.surface: Ironwork and copper fittings holding up rotten roof beams.
explanation.definitionFit: Base metals are common non-precious metals that corrode readily, such as iron and copper.

clue.text: Wind is immoderate, blowing one over?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the two letters of is are read backwards
blowing means losing, as in blowing a chance, so one of the round letters goes

parts.note: rococo describes immoderately ornate decoration
O looks like the figure for one, a ring

explanation.surface: A gale so excessive it knocks someone off their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like a reversal signal but is the definition; ROCOCO has three Os, and losing one leaves ROCCO.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dusty wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Use easels and drawing board?

parts.note: going back to the drawing board means beginning again

explanation.walkthrough: Easels are rests for artwork, so using them is to rest art; and going back to the drawing board means starting over.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin something afresh, as when a design fails and returns to the drawing board.

clue.text: Settled up having collected SP: it'll cover the fare

indicators.note: having collected means holding something inside
in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: lit means settled, as a bird lit on a branch
SP is slang for information, the starting price at the races; info means the same

explanation.surface: A punter pays out after collecting a starting-price bet, enough to cover the bus fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' means food here: foil wraps a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen foil is wrapped over food to cover it while it cooks or keeps.

clue.text: Solver's approach corrects mistake, swapping vowels

indicators.note: swapping vowels means the E and the I trade places

parts.note: mends it means corrects it, puts the mistake right

explanation.surface: A solver's method: fix the error by exchanging the vowels.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the E and I in MENDS IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a habitual mental attitude, the way a solver thinks about a problem.

clue.text: Mum is ahead of time, but not as close

indicators.note: but not means except for, so the named letters are left out

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, mum
early means ahead of time
read as the plural of the letter a, the two As

explanation.surface: Mum arrives early, but not quite as near as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is not a little word joining things but two letter As to be removed from MA IS EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as in close-fisted means stingy, unwilling to spend.

clue.text: Mass vote against retiring divides e.g. opera and ballet workers

indicators.note: divides means splits apart by going into, so the mass and vote go inside

parts.note: opera and ballet are examples of the arts
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the vote is read backwards

parts.note: a nay is a vote against

explanation.surface: A large vote opposing cuts splits the arts world.
explanation.definitionFit: Army ants are workers that march in huge foraging columns, like a soldier colony.

clue.text: See 21
What gets you down — dis or dat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the duck that supplies eiderdown feathers
second meaning: 'either' in a mock dialect where th becomes d, as in dis and dat

explanation.walkthrough: 'gets you down' sounds like depressing you, but it is the source of down feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a sea duck whose soft breast feathers fill quilts; dis or dat is either in mock dialect.

clue.text: Very bizarrely done around here, jam's on top of cream?!

definitions.text: here, jam's on top of cream?!

indicators.note: around means placed round something, so the shuffled letters go round the abbreviation
bizarrely means oddly, so the letters of done are put in a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cream tea done in a very strange way, with the jam spread on top of the cream.
explanation.walkthrough: In Devon, an English county, a cream tea scone gets cream first then jam; in neighbouring Cornwall it is the reverse, a long-running rivalry. 'bizarrely' makes DEON from done, and V goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This English county is the place where scones get cream first and jam on top.

clue.text: Considerable resistance on board ship

indicators.note: on board means inside a vessel, so the letter goes within the word

parts.note: big means large, considerable
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Passengers on a boat put up stiff opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged sailing vessel.

clue.text: Seeking post

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as in chasing, trying to get
second meaning: post as the prefix for later, following

explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like mail or a job, but here it is the Latin prefix for later.
explanation.definitionFit: To be after something is to pursue it, and the prefix post- means subsequent.

clue.text: "Time's reportedly on the side of the fairies", solvers stressed?

indicators.note: on the side of means placed next to, so the pieces are set side by side
reportedly means as spoken aloud, so a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: hours, the periods of time, possessive; said with a dropped h
elves are fairy folk

explanation.surface: A saying that time favours the fairy folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossword convention is that the setter addresses 'we' solvers; the answer is the emphatic form.
explanation.definitionFit: The emphatic reflexive pronoun used when 'we', the people solving, is stressed.

clue.text: Fair's Fair — alternative title for this picture?

definitions.text: Fair's Fair — alternative title for this picture?

parts.words: Fair's Fair — alternative title for this picture?
parts.note: fair can mean lawful and also light-haired, so a film title pairing the two senses

explanation.walkthrough: The film is a 2001 comedy starring Reese Witherspoon as a blonde law student; both its words can mean fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful and light-haired are both senses of fair, so the film title restates the phrase.
